title: RCS 104 - Intensive Care, Ventilation and Professional Practice

items.q: Do not attempt resuscitation order may be defined as
o: the volume of blood the heart pumps in a given period
the gradual withdrawal of breathing support as the patient recovers
a documented decision that resuscitation should not be started
placing a breathing tube again after it has been removed
items.s: Do not attempt resuscitation order: a documented decision that resuscitation should not be started. The other options describe Reintubation, Cardiac output, Weaning.

items.q: The statement “a machine that moves gas into the lungs of a patient” describes which of the following?
o: Barotrauma
Breath trigger
Atelectasis
Ventilator
items.s: Ventilator is a machine that moves gas into the lungs of a patient.

items.q: The statement “the pressure in the large veins, used to judge how well the heart is filling” describes which of the following?
o: Central venous pressure
Urine output
Haemodynamic monitoring
Capillary refill
items.s: Central venous pressure is the pressure in the large veins, used to judge how well the heart is filling.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Intensive care.
o: the pressure in the large veins, used to judge how well the heart is filling
the state of being unable to move, with risks to skin and muscle
the use of medicine to keep a patient calm and drowsy
the specialised care of patients whose lives are threatened by organ failure
items.s: Intensive care: the specialised care of patients whose lives are threatened by organ failure. The other options describe Immobility, Sedation, Central venous pressure.

items.q: The statement “chest compressions and rescue breaths given when the heart stops” describes which of the following?
o: Rescue breath
Defibrillation
Chain of survival
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
items.s: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation is chest compressions and rescue breaths given when the heart stops.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Intensive care?
o: a written plan of the care that a patient is to receive
the specialised care of patients whose lives are threatened by organ failure
the legal and moral obligation to protect those in one's care
having the knowledge and skill to perform a task safely
items.s: Intensive care: the specialised care of patients whose lives are threatened by organ failure. The other options describe Competence, Duty of care, Care plan.

items.q: Care plan may be defined as
o: the gradual withdrawal of breathing support as the patient recovers
a written plan of the care that a patient is to receive
widespread lung inflammation with fluid leaking into the alveoli
a period of breathing without support used to test readiness
items.s: Care plan: a written plan of the care that a patient is to receive. The other options describe Weaning, Acute respiratory distress syndrome, Spontaneous breathing trial.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Central venous pressure?
o: the pressure in the large veins, used to judge how well the heart is filling
a blood clot that travels to the lungs and blocks their circulation
the complete stopping of breathing, which needs immediate support
a period of breathing without support used to test readiness
items.s: Central venous pressure: the pressure in the large veins, used to judge how well the heart is filling. The other options describe Pulmonary embolism, Respiratory arrest, Spontaneous breathing trial.

a blood clot that travels to the lungs and blocks their circulation
the relief of pain without producing loss of consciousness
items.s: Analgesia: the relief of pain without producing loss of consciousness. The other options describe Shock, Pulmonary embolism, Sedation.

Negligence
Professional boundary
Scope of practice
items.s: Negligence is failure to give the standard of care that a patient is owed.

a note written at the time of the event it describes

a blood clot that travels to the lungs and blocks their circulation
items.s: Informed consent: agreement given after the patient understands the plan and its risks. The other options describe Pulmonary embolism, Contemporaneous record, Respiratory arrest.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Breath trigger.

items.s: Breath trigger: the signal, from patient or machine, that starts a breath. The other options describe Clinical record, Care plan, Situational awareness.

the legal and moral obligation to protect those in one's care
